quotes.text: “They called us on a Friday and said, ‘Hey, can you meet on Monday?’ So that’s how fast that happened,” Gochenour said, emphasizing the limited notice given to county officials.

quotes.text: “When they do all the digging, what will happen to our wells and our homes?” asked Joanna Gregory, a longtime Bedington resident.

“Don’t shoot the messenger,” Hardy said. “This is state level out of the governor’s office. We had no say in it.”
“I feel that the governor and the legislature should have a town hall. They’re the ones that voted for this law. Let them come explain it to the public,” Gochenour said.

facts: Berkeley County Commission discussed review process for incoming data centers at a regular Thursday meeting
House Bill 2014 puts control of data center approvals with the state, so developers need not follow county planning committee recommendations
Commissioners Jim Whitacre and H.D. Boyd agreed with Hardy against sending plans through the planning process
County planners are to develop a 'data center criteria' with best practices
HB2014, passed in 2025 at the urging of Governor Patrick Morrisey, exempts data centers from all local planning laws and ordinances and keeps their impact studies off the public record.
Penzance Management's planned data center campus in Berkeley County's Falling Waters District is $4 billion and 600 megawatts.
The Penzance Falling Waters project is the first project approved under HB2014.
Over 500 people attended a Berkeley County town hall on the proposed Bedington data center at Spring Mills High School
The 600-megawatt, $4 billion Bedington campus was announced by Gov. Patrick Morrisey and would bypass local zoning under House Bill 2014
Under HB 2014, 50% of tax proceeds reduce the state personal income tax and 30% stay in the host county
Commissioners did not directly respond to questions during the meeting; the governor's office did not respond to a request for comment

## Description

The company behind a hyperscale AI data center campus is offering to buy neighboring properties impacted by the construction. However, the mostly retired homeowners feel they’re being pushed out of the homes they’ve lived in for decades.

facts: House Bill 2014 established West Virginia's microgrid and data center certified program and exempts projects from county or municipal oversight including zoning and building permitting
The final version of HB 2014 sends 30% of high impact data center tax revenue to counties, versus an original draft sending all to state coffers
The House passed HB 2014 on April 1, 2025, 88 to 12, and the Legislature passed the final version April 12, 2025
Final law sends 30% of tax revenue from such projects to the host county and 5% divided across the other 54 counties
The bill removes local authority to restrict noise, lighting, land use, and regulate data centers and microgrids
Nearly 300 people attended a community meeting in Davis Volunteer Fire Hall on April 13, 2025
